days.title: Freestanding C and the Project Contract

questions.prompt: What does -ffreestanding establish for this kernel build?
options: The compiler cannot assume a hosted C environment with normal startup and the full library.
All undefined C behavior becomes architecture-defined.
The CPU begins in 64-bit mode.
Every external symbol is supplied by GRUB.
questions.explanation: Freestanding compilation removes hosted-environment assumptions. It does not initialize the machine, resolve symbols, or legalize undefined behavior.

questions.prompt: Why does ToyOS compile with -mno-red-zone?
options: To disable page-table writes.
To prevent compiler temporaries below RSP from being overwritten by asynchronous entry.
To make the stack grow upward.
To reserve space for Multiboot2 tags.
questions.explanation: The AMD64 red zone is unsafe for kernel code when interrupts or exceptions can use memory below the interrupted RSP.

questions.prompt: Which part of the kernel_main handoff belongs primarily to the System V AMD64 ABI?
options: The Multiboot2 magic value
The meaning of CR3
Placement of the first two integer arguments in EDI and ESI
The page-fault vector number
questions.explanation: Multiboot2 defines argument meaning, while the calling convention determines the C argument registers.

questions.prompt: What does a zero undefined-symbol count in the final ELF prove?
options: Every runtime path is correct.
The image boots on all x86-64 hardware.
No C operation has undefined behavior.
Static symbol references in that linked ELF were resolved.
questions.explanation: Link resolution is useful static evidence, but it is not runtime or platform validation.

questions.prompt: Why is ENTRY(_start) distinct from kernel_main?
options: The loader transfers to assembly that must establish machine and ABI state before C.
C functions cannot appear in ELF files.
GRUB calls every ELF symbol in order.
kernel_main is a page-table entry.
questions.explanation: The assembly entry handles the 32-bit protocol and transition before making an ABI-compliant C call.

questions.prompt: What is the best description of an ELF program header?
options: A C preprocessor include
Loader-facing segment metadata
A list of quiz questions
The x86 IDT
questions.explanation: Program headers describe segments for loading; sections primarily organize linking and analysis.

questions.prompt: What does the Multiboot2 checksum arrange?
options: The entire ISO hashes to zero.
Every loadable segment has equal size.
Magic, architecture, length, and checksum sum to zero modulo 2^32.
GRUB and ToyOS use the same GDT.
questions.explanation: That modular sum is part of header validation, not an integrity hash of the whole image.

questions.prompt: What does grub2-file recognition not prove?
options: That the inspected artifact looks like a Multiboot2 kernel to the tool
That a header was discoverable
That the file passed the command's check
That the image completed bootstrap and ran kernel_main
questions.explanation: Recognition is static. Execution needs dynamic boot evidence.

days.title: Long Mode, Initial Pages, GDT, and Stack

questions.prompt: What range do 512 identity-mapped 2 MiB PDEs cover?
options: The first 1 GiB
The first 2 MiB
The first 512 GiB
Only the 1 MiB kernel image
questions.explanation: 512 × 2 MiB equals 1 GiB, with virtual and physical addresses equal in this initial map.

questions.prompt: Why does ToyOS perform a far jump after enabling paging and long-mode support?
options: To clear CR3
To load a 64-bit code selector and enter the long-mode code path
To invoke GRUB again
To allocate the interrupt stack
questions.explanation: The far transfer loads CS from the bootstrap GDT and reaches 64-bit code.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a ToyOS implementation choice rather than an x86-64 requirement?
options: CR3 identifies paging structures.
EFER contains the long-mode enable bit.
The bootstrap identity maps exactly the first 1 GiB using 2 MiB pages.
A far transfer can load CS.
questions.explanation: The architecture supplies mechanisms; the mapping extent and page-size choice are project policy.

questions.prompt: Why does writing boot_magic to EDI fit the C signature?
options: EDI is the stack pointer.
Every architecture passes values in EDI.
Multiboot2 mandates the System V ABI.
The first AMD64 integer argument is RDI, and a 32-bit write supplies the uint32_t value.
questions.explanation: This is the internal bridge from saved protocol data to the chosen C calling convention.

questions.prompt: Why can ToyOS use serial_putc before interrupts are configured?
options: It polls the UART transmitter-ready status.
GRUB converts every call into a syscall.
The IDT transmits each byte.
The linker prints the bytes.
questions.explanation: Polling avoids dependence on an interrupt-driven serial path, though it can spin indefinitely.

questions.prompt: What mechanism does ASSERT(false) use?
options: An x86 page fault
A normal C branch into ToyOS panic policy
A hardware double fault
A Multiboot2 error code
questions.explanation: The assertion macro calls panic_at; it does not enter through the IDT.

questions.prompt: Why does the QEMU harness check both status and a serial marker?
options: Either value changes the ELF machine type.
The UART cannot print newlines.
Together they identify the intended path more narrowly than either alone.
The status is the page-fault address.
questions.explanation: A marker can precede a hang, and an exit can occur through the wrong path.

questions.prompt: What is not established by COM1 output under QEMU TCG?
options: The guest emitted matching bytes
The wrapper observed the expected marker
The selected execution reached serial_write
Physical UART timing on arbitrary hardware
questions.explanation: The device is emulated and connected to a host stream; physical timing is outside this evidence.

days.title: IDT, Exception Stubs, and a Uniform Saved Frame

questions.prompt: Why does ISR_NOERR push a synthetic zero?
options: To give vectors without a CPU error code the same vector/error frame shape.
To clear CR2.
To acknowledge the PIC.
To select IST zero.
questions.explanation: Normalization lets the common entry and C structure use one layout.

questions.prompt: Why is r15 the first field of interrupt_frame although RAX is pushed first?
options: C reverses every structure.
The downward-growing stack points at the last pushed register, R15.
R15 stores the IDT base.
The compiler alphabetizes registers.
questions.explanation: After all pushes, RSP addresses R15, so the structure follows memory order from that address upward.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of cld before calling interrupt_handler?
options: Disable interrupts
Clear debug registers
Restore the ABI expectation that the direction flag is clear
Load the data selector
questions.explanation: Exception entry can interrupt code with DF set; C code expects the ABI's forward direction.

questions.prompt: What does the successful int3 self-test exercise that a non-returning fault does not?
options: Multiboot2 header discovery
Initial page-table construction
UART divisor setup only
Register restoration and iretq back to the interrupted flow
questions.explanation: The breakpoint handler returns, so the assembly unwind and architectural return path are exercised.

days.title: TSS, IST, Page Faults, and GDB Diagnosis

questions.prompt: What does ToyOS primarily use its 64-bit TSS for?
options: Supplying privilege and IST stack pointers
Hardware scheduling of Week 7 tasks
Storing the ELF symbol table
Formatting serial numbers
questions.explanation: The loaded TSS supplies stack-selection metadata; ToyOS does not use hardware task switching.

questions.prompt: Why should the write to 0x70000000 fault in the Week 6 profile?
options: It is inside the serial I/O range.
It lies beyond the initial first-1-GiB mapping.
Every volatile store is forbidden.
The GDT marks all data read-only.
questions.explanation: The initial identity map ends at 0x3fffffff, so the selected linear address has no present translation.

questions.prompt: Which evidence trio best diagnoses this x86 page fault?
options: GRUB menu, baud rate, and ISO size
GDT limit, compiler version, and PIT divisor
CR2 address, page-fault error code, and saved RIP
Only the panic string
questions.explanation: Address, access classification, and instruction context are complementary.

questions.prompt: Why must GDB load build/week6-page/toyos.elf for the fault VM?
options: GDB can debug only files named week6-page.
The normal ELF contains no x86 instructions.
QEMU reads source through GDB.
Symbols and source mapping must correspond to the exact fault-profile binary.
questions.explanation: Using another build can map saved addresses to incorrect symbols or lines.

days.title: Integrated Fault-Debug Report and Systems Comparison

questions.prompt: Which wording most accurately reports objdump evidence?
options: objdump decoded these bytes as the shown x86-64 instruction.
The instruction executed on every physical CPU.
The C standard requires this exact opcode.
Linux generated the instruction.
questions.explanation: Disassembly is static decoding of an artifact; execution and universal code generation need separate evidence.

questions.prompt: What is the closest conceptual xv6-riscv counterpart to ToyOS's interrupt_frame?
options: A disk inode
A trapframe/register save area
A page allocator bitmap
The Makefile
questions.explanation: Both preserve interrupted register context, although architecture fields and entry mechanisms differ.

questions.prompt: Which comparison between ToyOS and Linux is justified?
options: ToyOS implements Linux demand paging.
Linux x86 uses the exact ToyOS C structure.
Both layer architecture entry, saved state, dispatch, and policy, while Linux is far more complete.
ToyOS and Linux have identical per-CPU entry stacks.
questions.explanation: The conceptual layers correspond, but concrete structures, recovery, concurrency, and policy differ substantially.

questions.prompt: Which item belongs in the limitations section of the Week 6 report?
options: The observed page-fault marker
The exact ELF hash
The predicted vector
No user-mode, nested-fault, or physical-hardware behavior was tested
questions.explanation: A report must bound its claims to the tested QEMU profiles and explicitly name important untested cases.
